Tau isoform mapping across tissues and biofluids reveals a signature distinguishing Alzheimer’s disease from amyotrophic lateral sclerosis
articles.abstract: Abstract Blood phosphorylated tau 217 (p-tau217) accurately detects Alzheimer’s disease (AD) pathology but is also elevated in amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), likely reflecting peripheral (big) tau released from muscle. Assays selectively measuring brain-derived (BD-) tau and BD-p-tau217 are therefore needed. We analysed serum BD-tau and p-tau217 in ALS ( n = 139), AD ( n = 101) and controls ( n = 75) using direct immunoassays and after BD-Tau immunoprecipitation (BD-Tau-IP), and tau species in brain ( n = 16), spinal cord ( n = 11) and muscle ( n = 10) by targeted mass spectrometry. With the direct immunoassays, BD-tau and p-tau217 were increased in AD and ALS versus controls. After BD-Tau-IP, BD-tau and BD-p-tau217 were elevated in AD only, improving diagnostic accuracy. Mass spectrometry revealed a central-to-peripheral shift from BD-tau to big tau predominance, with exclusively big p-tau217 detected in muscle. Selective detection of BD-tau species improves the specificity of blood AD biomarkers by reducing peripheral tau confounding.

articles.title: Trans-ancestry genome-wide association meta-analysis of gallstone disease
articles.abstract: Abstract Gallstone disease is a highly prevalent and costly gastrointestinal disease. Yet, genetic variation in gallstone susceptibility and its implication in metabolic pathways remain to be explored. We report a trans-ancestry genome-wide association meta-analysis of gallstone disease including 100,856 cases and 1,596,602 controls in the UK Biobank, FinnGen, Biobank Japan, and Million Veteran Program. We identified 116 (59 novel) risk loci across meta-analysis and found replication in statistically compelling signals in the All of Us Research Program. A polygenic risk score constructed from trans-ancestry lead variants was positively associated with liver chemistry and alpha-1-antitrypsin deficiency and negatively associated with total cholesterol and low-density lipoprotein levels among trans-ancestry and European ancestry groups in the Penn Medicine BioBank. Colocalization of risk loci with 44 traits and with expression quantitative trait loci from eight tissues yielded 321 and 110 significant colocalizations, respectively. These findings broaden our understanding of the genetic architecture of gallstone disease.

articles.title: Topology and evolution of global transcriptional regulatory networks across the Klebsiella pneumoniae pan-genome
Deconvoluting the mode of action of antileishmanial aminopyrazoles through chemical mutagenesis
Light-powered photosynthetic living actuator
Reduced-DSP 200G/λ low-voltage slow-light silicon modulator enabled by built-in EO equalizer
articles.abstract: Abstract Multi-Tb/s optical interconnects for artificial intelligence data centers necessitate high-speed, energy-efficient, and compact transceivers. However, conventional silicon Mach-Zehnder modulators are fundamentally limited by low modulation efficiency and large physical dimensions that typically extend several millimeters, requiring high-swing drivers and power-intensive digital signal processing to achieve data rates exceeding 100 Gb/s per lane. Here we show a silicon photonic crystal waveguide slow-light modulator that overcomes the bandwidth-efficiency trade-off via a built-in electro-optic equalizer. By monolithically integrating optical delay lines and crossings within segmented slow-light phase shifters, we synthesized an on-chip feedforward response that extends the 3-dB bandwidth. The fabricated modulator with a small device length of 320 µm demonstrated 140-Gb/s on-off keying operation with an energy consumption of 26 fJ/bit using drive voltages compatible with fin field-effect transistor-based complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor technology. Furthermore, four-level pulse amplitude modulation achieved 180 Gb/s without digital signal processing and 200 Gb/s with a low-complexity 11-tap digital equalizer. By reducing reliance on power-dissipating electronics, this strategy provides a potential route toward future dense multi-Tb/s co-packaged optics for energy-constrained switching systems.

articles.title: Non-polar surface passivation of PbS Quantum Dots using metal thiolates enables photodiodes rivaling InGaAs performance
articles.abstract: Abstract Colloidal quantum dots (CQDs) short-wave infrared (SWIR) detectors (1-2 µm) are of great interest for a plethora of applications including autonomous driving, machine vision, night and adverse weather imaging, in view of their low-cost and compatibility to read-out electronics. However, to date, CQDs photodetectors still suffer from high dark current and thereby noise such that their performance remains inferior to epitaxially grown III-V semiconductors. This performance gap originates from the limited passivation of non-polar surfaces existent in large PbS CQDs needed to access the SWIR spectral range. Here we report on a lead-thiolate based chemistry that serves to passivate both polar and non-polar surfaces of PbS CQDs yielding inks with unprecedented optoelectronic quality evidenced by open circuit voltage deficit and dark current activation energies matching those of single crystalline semiconductors. As a result, we demonstrate infrared photodetectors with remarkable thermal resilience, very low dark current density ( ~ 34 nA cm −2 at −1 V) and a specific detectivity D* of ~8×10 12 Jones. The measured D* value is on par with that of commercially available InGaAs photodiodes (PDs).

articles.title: NHEJ-mediated DNA synapsis and RPA-driven MRX exonuclease balance DNA end resection to control DSB repair
articles.abstract: Abstract DNA double-strand breaks (DSBs) are repaired by Ku-dependent non-homologous end-joining (NHEJ) or DNA end resection-dependent homologous recombination (HR). Previously, it was shown that short-range resection by MRX-pSae2 can remove Ku from DSBs and initiate resection, showing flexibility in DSB repair pathway choice. However, which NHEJ intermediates can be disrupted by resection factors remains unknown. Using reconstituted reactions with purified S. cerevisiae proteins, we show here that short-range resection by MRX-pSae2 is not directly inhibited by any of the core NHEJ factors. Instead, we find that MRX-pSae2 is inhibited structurally. DNA synapsis, a dynamic NHEJ intermediate that bridges DSBs, strongly suppresses resection. Non-ligatable ends are refractory to MRX-pSae2 once synapsis formed, and NHEJ assemblies with catalytic mutants of DNA ligase IV that permit synapsis but do not allow ligation likewise inhibit resection. We further demonstrate that removal of Ku from DSBs requires RPA, which interacts with MRX and pSae2 to synergistically stimulate MRX 3′−5′ exonuclease activity, generating free 3′ overhangs. Our data support a model in which DNA synapsis temporarily prevents resection, allowing NHEJ to execute ligation. If ligation fails and synapsis dissociates, MRX-pSae2 and RPA promote resection that removes non-productive NHEJ assemblies and channels DSB repair toward HR. The data help explain the suppression of NHEJ by RPA observed in previous genetic experiments.

articles.title: Laser-enhanced quantum sensing boosts sensitivity and dynamic range
articles.abstract: Abstract While magnetometers based on nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers in diamond have emerged as the most important solid-state quantum sensors, ensembles are typically limited to a few percent optical contrast. Here, we demonstrate a laser threshold magnetometry-based NV system that achieves 100% optical contrast in combination with strong output signals up to 50 mW. By integrating the NV centers into a laser cavity, we show magnetic-field-dependent shifts of the laser threshold, allowing the laser system to be entirely switched off with the NV centers’ magnetic resonance. We determine the photon-shot-noise fundamental sensitivity limit to be < 400 fT/ $$\sqrt{{{\rm{Hz}}}}$$ Hz for all vector components and demonstrate that it improves super-linearly with contrast. This sensitivity is not achieved at the usual cost of smaller linewidth, i.e., maintains good intrinsic dynamic range. This provides a perspective for highly sensitive magnetometry operated outside magnetically-shielded rooms for applications including magnetoencephalography, magnetic navigation, and magnetic anomaly detection.

articles.title: Ocean acidification, reduced silicate availability and declines in Ocean productivity
XIST drives X-chromosome inactivation and safeguards female extraembryonic cells in humans
articles.abstract: Abstract X-chromosome inactivation (XCI) is essential for extraembryonic tissue growth and embryo development in mice. However, species-specific differences in its timing and regulation have left its role in human development unclear. Here, we show that the in vitro differentiation of naive human pluripotent stem cells to trophoblast stem cells and extraembryonic mesoderm cells is accompanied by XCI. The inactive X chromosome displays an atypical chromatin state, lacking DNA methylation and canonical heterochromatin marks. We demonstrate that extraembryonic differentiation and XCI are temporally linked. Using loss of function approaches, we found that XIST is required for XCI establishment in humans. Furthermore, we show that XCI is needed for the survival of human female extraembryonic cells. Together, these findings link XCI to the formation of human extraembryonic lineages, with important implications for human reproductive biology.

articles.title: Single-Cell Insights into Size-Dependent Heterogeneous Bioconcentration and Distribution of Metal Species Ranging from Ions to Nanoclusters and Nanoparticles in Chlorella vulgaris
articles.abstract: Abstract Particle size is a key factor influencing metal uptake by aquatic unicellular primary producers. To investigate size-dependent bioconcentration ranging from ions to nanoclusters (NCs) and nanoparticles (NPs), we used cytometry by time-of-flight (CyTOF) to quantitatively examine single-cell uptake, retention, and bioconcentration in Chlorella vulgaris exposed to Au3+ ions, three glutathione (GSH)-protected AuNC preparations (Au10–12SG10–12, Au15SG13, and Au25SG18), and four GSH-coated AuNPs (5, 15, 25, 50 nm). Au3+ and AuNCs showed rapid cell-associated accumulation but followed exponential-decay and two-phase clearance kinetics, indicating efficient cellular elimination and a tendency to be released back into the medium. In contrast, AuNPs followed saturation-type bioconcentration kinetics, with larger particles showing more persistent cell association. Single-cell analysis revealed strong size-dependent heterogeneity: under equal-mass exposure, the fraction of Au-positive cells decreased exponentially with increasing atom number, whereas the Au burden per Au-positive cell increased approximately linearly. Larger particles exhibited higher volume concentration factors (VCFs) with a small subset of “high-VCF” cells. These results highlight that both particle size and cellular heterogeneity jointly govern algal bioconcentration patterns and should be accounted for in environmental risk assessment of metal-based nanomaterials.

articles.title: Integrating Lattice and Molecular Oxygen Pathways to Enhance Toluene Oxidation via Mn Substitution in Fe x Co3– x O4 Spinel
articles.abstract: Abstract Activation of lattice oxygen and molecular oxygen critically governs the catalytic degradation of volatile organic compounds (VOCs), driving substantial research into harmonizing the bonding state of oxygen atoms in transition-metal oxides to facilitate VOCs abatement. However, the underlying mechanism of oxygen activation via cation substitution in spinel remains to be explored owing to its significant flexibility in both tetrahedral and octahedral sites. Herein, a Mn-substituted FexCo3–xO4 spinel catalyst was developed for promoting oxidation of toluene (one of the typical aromatic VOCs), with the temperature of 90% toluene conversion decreasing by approximately 51 °C relative to the pristine one. Multiple characterizations and theoretical calculations revealed that Mn3+ substitution at octahedral Co3+ sites of FexCo3–xO4 modulated the metal–oxygen bonds within the Mn–O–Co structure for activating surface lattice oxygen, accompanied by the creation of abundant oxygen vacancies for O2 excitation. The combined results of temperature-programmed analyses, isotopic labeling experiments, and in situ spectroscopy showed that the adsorbed toluene could be synchronously oxidized by activated lattice oxygen and chemisorbed oxygen generated via O2 activation, thereby accomplishing the deep oxidation of toluene. This study clarifies the synergistic role of lattice and molecular oxygen in toluene oxidation and affords a potential catalyst for environmental remediation.

articles.title:
Absolute Environmental
Sustainability Assessment:
From Academia to Decision Support in Industry and Government

Building
Resilience
into Large-Scale Seawater Desalination

Early Life Stage
Exposure to Environmentally Relevant
Concentrations of TCPP Induces Multigenerational Reproductive Toxicity
in Estuarine Fish: A Study Based on Whole-Genome Methylation and Steroidogenesis
Pathway
articles.abstract: Abstract Tris (1-chloro-2-propyl) phosphate (TCPP) is ubiquitous in estuarine environments. Parental TCPP exposure impaired reproduction and offspring developmental in zebrafish; yet its multigenerational and transgenerational effects and epigenetic mechanisms in estuarine fish remain unknown. Here, Mugilogobius chulae embryos were exposed to TCPP until 25 days posthatching and reared in clean seawater until F2 hatching. Reproductive and gonadal end points were assessed across generations, while gonadal steroidogenesis and whole-body DNA methylation in larvae were analyzed in F0 and F1 to investigate potential endocrine and epigenetic mechanisms. TCPP induced multigenerational reproductive toxicity that was transmitted to F2 embryos, with F1 and F2 lowest observed effect concentrations 1 order of magnitude lower than that in F0. In F0, 100 μg/L TCPP reduced fecundity and male gonadosomatic index. In F1, 10, and 100 μg/L prolonged spawning latency and affected male gonadal development. In F2, 10 μg/L reduced embryonic hatching. Disruption of steroidogenesis gene expression and hormone levels occurred in F0 and F1 male gonads but only in F1 females. Whole-genome DNA methylation revealed persistent hypermethylation of nerve growth factor receptor (NGFR) and calcium voltage-gated channel auxiliary subunit γ 2 (CACNG2) in the mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) pathway across F0 and F1. Their hypermethylation and reduced expression were associated with decreased steroidogenic acute regulatory protein (STAR) and cytochrome P450 family 11 subfamily A member (CYP11A) in male gonads, suggesting NGFR and CACNG2 may represent candidate epigenetically regulated genes associated with TCPP-induced multigenerational reproductive toxicity. This study reveals transgenerational risks of environmental concentrations of TCPP to estuarine fish and provides epigenetic evidence for multigenerational endocrine disruptors.

articles.title:
Bioinspired
Phototropic
Endogenous Heating for Low-Temperature
Biological Wastewater Treatment
articles.abstract: Abstract Biological wastewater treatment in cold regions faces a low-efficiency and high-energy paradox due to low-temperature inhibition. Inspired by plant phototropism, this study reports bioinspired phototropic endogenous heating (Bio-PEH) based on the underwater opto-thermomechanical response. Upon illumination, cryopolymerized macroporous reduced graphene oxide@poly(N-isopropylacrylamide) fibers undergo asymmetric contraction, which reorients the illuminated surface to be normal to the light vector, so as to maximize photothermal flux under oblique incidence. Meanwhile, flash heating further enhances water-confined heat transfer and expands the effective heating domain. Bio-PEH arrays raise bulk wastewater from 7.8 to 30.2 °C, which improves NH4+ removal by 2.8-fold, accounting for 25.3–169.7% enhancement compared with Joule heating (JH), direct solar heating (DH), and static endogenous heating (SEH). Global simulations further indicate multifold thermal compensation at high latitudes with substantial carbon and energy cost reduction. This study provides a biophysically inspired strategy by utilizing opto-thermomechanical response to realize heating of low-temperature wastewater, making wastewater treatment in cold regions more efficient, economical, and sustainable.

articles.title: Concentration‑dependent switching between ligand‑like and solvent‑like lipid regulation in a model ion channel
articles.abstract: Abstract Cell membranes are not only protective barriers but also active chemical environments that regulate protein structure and function. However, how individual lipid species influence membrane proteins across physiological concentration ranges, either as specific ligands or through bilayer-mediated solvent effects, remains poorly defined. Here, using the cyclic nucleotide-gated ion channel SthK reconstituted into defined membranes, we show that phosphatidic acid enhances channel activity across all tested concentrations but, at low mole fractions ( ~ 0.7-1 mol%), it selectively and cooperatively increases agonist potency, meeting criteria for a site‑specific allosteric ligand. In contrast, the zwitterionic lipid phosphatidylethanolamine modulates SthK activity exclusively through linear, solvent‑like effects across the same concentration range. Structural analysis reveals that low anionic lipid content expands the closed‑state conformational ensemble without promoting pore opening, providing a structural basis for lipid-dependent latent allostery. Together, these results establish lipid concentration as a governing regulatory variable that quantitatively distinguishes ligand‑like from solvent‑like mechanisms of membrane protein regulation.

articles.title: High-content morphological profiling by Cell Painting in 3D spheroids
articles.abstract: Abstract Cell Painting is a popular high-content imaging assay that captures the shape and internal organization of 2D cell cultures at scale. While 3D cell cultures are more physiologically relevant models – especially for studying drug perturbations – they remain challenging to image because light scatters before it reaches the cultures’ interior. Here, we introduce a scalable method to adapt Cell Painting for 3D spheroids. We show that tissue-clearing, a technique that makes spheroids transparent, combined with a focusing routine that locates spheroids on the fly, enables Cell Painting at single-cell level inside intact spheroids. By profiling 52 clinically relevant drugs, we show that single-cell fingerprints clustered by biological pathway and resolved drug effects more robustly than those of flattened spheroid-wide views. Notably, the effect of two drugs, 5-fluorouracil and olaparib, nearly indistinguishable in 2D monolayers, diverged in spheroids. This finding was then corroborated by DNA-damage, cell-cycle, and gene-expression assays. The workflow runs on a spinning-disk confocal microscope in a standard 384-well plate format, making single-cell 3D profiling accessible to laboratories already performing Cell Painting.

articles.title:
From Equality to
Equity: The Dual Socioeconomic Inequalities
of Mobility-Based Exposure and Exposure Avoidance Options during Urban
Floods
articles.abstract: Abstract Urban pluvial flooding creates unequal risks that are not fully captured by residence-based exposure measures. We developed a framework that jointly evaluates mobility-based flood exposure (MFE) and exposure avoidance constraint (EAC), defined as the additional travel distance required to reduce flood susceptibility. Within Beijing’s Fifth Ring Road, we combined AlphaEarth Foundation Embeddings with mobile phone signaling data to quantify flood exposure and flood-avoidance routing constraints for 614,510 residents. EAC is measured by constructing Pareto frontiers through Monte Carlo path simulation, while multinomial logit models with interaction terms are used to examine the relationships between socioeconomic status (SES) and the dual inequalities. The results show: (1) residence-based assessment suffers from the Neighborhood Effect Averaging Problem, leading to systematic bias relative to mobility-based measures; (2) low-SES groups experience dual disadvantages, characterized by higher MFE and higher EAC; and (3) the interaction between exposure and avoidance constraint is state-dependent, reinforcing the relative disadvantage of low-SES residents beyond an additive pattern under finite EAC, while limiting further socioeconomic differentiation under infinite EAC. We argue for a shift from an equality-oriented to an equity-oriented perspective, providing actionable insights for disaster risk reduction and the achievement of SDGs 3, 10, and 11.

articles.title:
Establishing
an
Air Health Index for Predicting the
Risk of Acute Myocardial Infarction Onset Associated with Air Pollution
and Ambient Temperature
articles.abstract: Abstract Air pollutants and ambient temperature are important cardiovascular disease determinants, and communicating their overall risk is important for cardiovascular patient management. We developed a composite Air Health Index (AHI) by linking high-resolution exposure data with 1,207,625 acute myocardial infarction (AMI) cases across 325 Chinese cities. The AHI for AMI aggregates excess morbidity risks from fine particulate matter, nitrogen dioxide, ozone, and ambient temperature into a normalized scale (0–10+). Compared with existing metrics, the AHI for AMI showed better predictive performance for AMI onset than the Air Quality Index (AQI) and Air Quality Health Index (AQHI). Each interquartile range increase in the AHI for AMI was associated with a 5.97% (95% confidence interval [CI]: 5.32%–6.63%) increase in AMI incidence, surpassing the AQHI (3.33%, 95% CI: 2.93%–3.72%) and AQI (2.04%, 95% CI: 1.73%–2.35%). The AHI for AMI showed a nearly linear exposure–response relationship with no evident threshold and accounted for 8,534 per 100,000 AMI cases nationally. These associations were consistently validated in an independent external data set, supporting the robustness and generalizability of the index. In conclusion, the AHI for AMI provides an integrative and practical framework for assessing environmental health risks, offering actionable guidance for cardiovascular patient management.

articles.title:
Paternal
Preconception Calcitriol Intervention Rescued
DBDPE-Induced Transgenerational Developmental and Visual Toxicity
in Zebrafish
articles.abstract: Abstract Growing evidence highlights the impact of preconception paternal environmental exposures on offspring health, yet the specific paternal contributions and transgenerational mechanisms of emerging contaminants remain poorly understood. Thus, we exposed male zebrafish to decabromodiphenyl ethane (DBDPE), a widely used replacement for legacy flame retardants, for 2 months to investigate its intergenerational (F1) and transgenerational (F2) effects. Paternal DBDPE exposure severely impaired sperm quality in F0 zebrafish, and induced transgenerational developmental toxicity with elevated malformations in F2 larvae. Moreover, significant eye malformations occurred even at low doses in F2 groups, revealing the visual system to be highly sensitive to transgenerational DBDPE toxicity. F1 and F2 larvae exhibited marked behavioral disorders, retinal thinning, and phototransduction gene dysregulation, indicating significant visual dysfunction. Notably, transcriptome analysis revealed that steroid biosynthesis (especially calcitriol synthesis) was consistently disrupted across dose levels and generations, with its enrichment factor progressively increasing from F1 to F2; this was accompanied by a pronounced deficiency of calcitriol in paternal F0 testes. Accordingly, paternal calcitriol supplementation during DBDPE exposure effectively restored F0 sperm quality and mitigated visual and developmental toxicity in offspring. These findings suggest that paternal exposure to emerging contaminants may induce intergenerational and transgenerational effects, and that targeted preconception nutritional intervention may reduce these risks.

articles.title:
Adaptation
and Resistance
of Nitrifiers to Harsh Engineered
Conditions during Partial Nitritation
articles.abstract: Abstract Selective suppression of nitrite-oxidizing bacteria (NOB) is essential for stable partial nitritation (PN), yet NOB often persist or recover under engineered suppression conditions. This study investigated the kinetic, microbial, and genomic responses of NOB and ammonia-oxidizing bacteria (AOB) in a PN system subjected to low pH and high free nitrous acid (FNA) sidestream treatment. A sequencing batch reactor was operated for 283 days under varying treatment intensities. Long-term operation selectively enriched a Candidatus nitrotogafabula-related MAG (bin.69), characterized by a relatively high apparent growth rate (∼1.3 d–1) and low substrate affinity (Ks = 2.3 ± 0.4 mg NO2–-N L–1; Ko = 1.1 ± 0.3 mg O2 L–1). Comparative genomic analyses identified stress-tolerance-associated traits related to proton transport, ion homeostasis, protein stabilization, and cellular stress responses. Proteome isoelectric (pI) point analysis further showed a lower genomic pI profile than other known NOB, potentially consistent with persistence under acidic and FNA stress. These findings provide genome-informed insights into NOB persistence under long-term suppression and implications for improving PN stability.

articles.title:
Emissions
of Respirable Magnetite from the Coal-Fired
Power Sector in China: Spatial Inequalities and Mitigation Pathways
articles.abstract: Abstract Magnetite particles, being ubiquitous and highly abundant in the atmosphere, have raised notable cardiovascular and neurodegenerative health risks globally. However, the limited understanding of their emissions hinders the targeted mitigation. Here, we developed a multifactor emission modeling framework to evaluate magnetite emission from the coal-fired power sector in China, one of the most sizable contributors to airborne magnetite, and identify policy-effective mitigation pathways. Total atmospheric emissions of respirable magnetite are 2,828.7 (2,307.1–3,371.4) t per year, exhibiting distinct spatial inequalities driven by tiered emission standards. Despite contributing only 4% of national coal-fired power, two superemitting provinces, Guizhou and Sichuan, could reduce over 31% of the national magnetite emission by tightening their emission standards, highlighting that targeting hotspots regions represents a highly efficient pathway to substantial mitigation benefits. These findings can facilitate policy-making for achieving targeted magnetite mitigation and provide transferable insight for air pollution control in other countries globally.

articles.title: Emission Mitigation and Climate Warming Increase China’s Ozone Responsiveness to Soil NO x Relative to Biogenic VOCs
articles.abstract: Abstract Surface ozone (O3) remains a major air quality challenge in China despite recent reductions in anthropogenic emissions. Here, we use regional photochemical modeling to quantify changes in summertime O3 responses to relative perturbations in biogenic volatile organic compounds (BVOCs) and soil nitrogen oxides (NOx) under historical emission conditions and future mitigation and climate scenarios through 2060. Declining anthropogenic emissions increase ozone production efficiency and produce divergent response patterns: the modeled O3 response magnitude to BVOCs perturbations generally decreases, whereas the response magnitude to soil NOx perturbations increases. Under the 2060 net-zero scenario, the O3 response to an equivalent relative perturbation in soil NOx exceeds that to BVOCs in several regions. Projected climate warming further enhances O3 responsiveness to soil NOx, particularly in agriculturally intensive regions. These results indicate a scenario-dependent shift in the relative O3-response magnitude to natural precursor emissions, rather than a direct change in their source contributions. The increasing responsiveness to soil NOx suggests that agricultural nitrogen management should be evaluated as a potential complement to conventional industrial and transportation emission controls in future ozone mitigation strategies.

articles.title:
Monitoring the Environmental
Degradation of Biodegradable
Mulch Films Using Py-GC-MS and a Multitechnique Analytical Approach
articles.abstract: Abstract Biodegradable mulch films have been developed for use in agriculture to reduce costs incurred during the retrieval of conventional mulch films and to prevent plastic pollution of soil caused by their incomplete removal. However, there are knowledge gaps on their degradation rate and potential environmental impact of any residuals. This study investigated the degradation of three commercially available mulch films, one made of polyethylene and two labeled as “biodegradable”. These products were exposed to four conditions in the open environment. After 24 months in soil, air, and a combination of air pre-exposure for 3 months followed by soil burial, all samples retained their overall film structure and were still recoverable, although different levels of physical and chemical changes indicated ongoing degradation. In seawater, no residual fragments of the biodegradable mulch films remained after 3 months of exposure. Pyrolysis-gas chromatography-mass spectrometry detected leaching of a plasticizer from one of the biodegradable films in all environments and other degradation features. The outcome of this study highlights the potential for environmental accumulation of mulch films labeled as “biodegradable” and the need for the development of international environmental testing standards and associated labeling to guide users on appropriate use and disposal of mulch films.

articles.title:
Global
Cropland
Efficiency-Stress Divide: Typological
Diagnosis and Reconciling Pathways
articles.abstract: Abstract Cropland underpins food security but faces mounting resource constraints and environmental pressures. Achieving sustainable agriculture hinges on advancing land use efficiency (LUE) and alleviating land ecological stress (LES). However, a typological framework characterizing LUE and LES remains lacking, hindering the distinction between technical efficiency and ecological sustainability in cropland use. Herein, we establish a coupled LUE-LES diagnostic framework by integrating the super-efficiency slack-based measure model with land ecological footprint accounting. This framework classifies regions into efficiency-stress typologies globally for 2011, 2015, 2019, and 2022, and identifies type-specific improvement priorities through slack and ecological footprint-biocapacity diagnostics. Results show that in 2022, LUE is below 1 in 62.5% of regions, while China and Brazil reach 1.90 and 1.81, respectively, but remain efficient-stressed due to high ecological deficits. Despite ecological deficits, Indonesia and Australia exhibit the highest outflow intensity of embodied cropland use, exporting 55.9% and 68.0% of regional production-based land ecological footprint (PLEF), respectively. Two-dimensional diagnostics identify irrigation water and energy as dominant sources of inefficiency and show that PLEF exceeds land biocapacity by approximately 5%–35% in deficit regions. Policy designs for reconciling LUE and LES should guide supply-side efficiency gains, complemented by demand- and trade-oriented measures for durable agricultural sustainability.

articles.title:
The New Frontiers
in Endocrine Disruption Research
and Policy
articles.abstract: Abstract Since the 1991 Wingspread Consensus Statement, the field of endocrine disruption has emerged as a distinct and complex area that continues to challenge conventional approaches to toxicology and risk assessment. Nonetheless, despite substantial scientific advances, including the identification of over 1,000 Endocrine Disrupting Chemicals (EDCs), the description of nonmonotonic dose–response relationships, and the elucidation of multiple mechanisms of action, regulatory progress continues to lag. Recent stagnation in research investment into EDCs reflects a persistent tension between robust scientific evidence and policy implementation for environmental chemicals, which is especially salient for those bearing the unique properties and concerns of endocrine disruptors. In this article, we delineate the lull in EDC research that began in the mid-to-late 2010s and discuss how per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) have refocused public, scientific, and regulatory attention away from EDCs. While PFAS qualify as EDCs, their structural similarity and environmental persistence enable regulatory pathways that circumvent traditional research bottlenecks confronting other endocrine disruptors. This divergence presents both opportunities and potential drawbacks: while PFAS regulation may revitalize the broader EDC field, overemphasis on PFAS could perpetuate longstanding challenges in chemical prioritization, mixture assessment, and cumulative risk evaluation. We highlight state-level initiatives in Maine, Minnesota, and Washington as promising models for adaptive regulation. Moving forward, coordinated action among states, industry, academia, and civil society will be essential to advancing protective EDC policy while maintaining scientific rigor and feasibility.

articles.title:
Surface-Confined
Pt–Ov–Mn
Atomic Interfaces Promote Deep Benzene Mineralization through Coupled
Electron Transfer and Lattice-Oxygen Activation
articles.abstract: Abstract Single-atom catalysts are promising for VOC abatement, but their application is limited by the trade-off between the stability of isolated atoms and the redox activity. Herein, we report a surface-confined Pt–Ov–Mn atomic interface constructed within the outer layer of Mn2O3 via thermal self-reconstruction. Oxygen vacancies trap isolated Pt atoms and electronically connect them with neighboring Mn centers, forming a vacancy-rich interfacial active center. For benzene oxidation, Pt1/Mn2O3 achieved a specific reaction rate of 45.70 μmol gPt–1 s–1 at 140 °C, which is 3.8 and 11.2 times those of the Pt nanocluster and nanoparticle counterparts, respectively. The catalyst also exhibited excellent thermal stability and enhanced tolerance to SO2 poisoning. Mechanistic studies reveal that the Pt–Ov–Mn interface enables electron–lattice-oxygen coupling: interfacial Pt 5d–Mn 3d electronic interaction upshifts the Pt d-band center, strengthening benzene π adsorption and promoting C–H activation and ring opening, while adjacent oxygen vacancies accelerate lattice-oxygen migration and replenishment through a Mars–van Krevelen cycle. This coupled pathway suppresses the accumulation of partially oxidized intermediates and drives deep mineralization to CO2. These findings identify surface-layer atomic interfaces as designable active centers for developing robust SACs toward hazardous VOC control.

articles.title:
Atmospheric
Observations
Reveal the Spatial Influence
of Inland Shipping Channels and Enhanced Emission Signals from AIS-Unmatched
Vessels
articles.abstract: Abstract Inland shipping is an important but poorly constrained source of urban air pollution, particularly in dense waterway networks, where vessel activity records are incomplete. Here, we integrate high-time-resolution differential optical absorption spectroscopy (DOAS), national air-quality observations, meteorological normalization, spatial exposure analysis, automatic identification system (AIS) records, and field photographs to evaluate inland shipping impacts in two representative channel environments in eastern China. SO2 showed stronger spatial heterogeneity than nitrogen-related pollutants and was more closely associated with the nearby shipping channels. After meteorological normalization, inland-waterway configuration explained 44% of the interstation variability in urban SO2, with the strongest association at an influence distance of approximately 4 km. Event-scale analysis revealed frequent short-term pollutant enhancements associated with the vessel passages. However, only 54.4% of plume events at the open-channel station and 44.8% at the lock-controlled site could be matched to AIS-recorded vessels. AIS-unmatched plume events were not negligible and, in the lock-controlled environment, were associated with SO2 signals higher than those of AIS-matched events. These results demonstrate that atmospheric observations provide an independent constraint on underdetected inland shipping emissions and suggest that inventories relying solely on vessel activity records may underestimate or mischaracterize sulfur-related emissions from inland waterways.

articles.title:
Efficient Formation
of Atmospheric Triplets and Organosulfur
from Photochemistry of Non/weakly Light-absorbing Biomass Burning
Tracers and S(IV)
articles.abstract: Abstract Biomass burning (BB) events emit S(IV) and biomass-burning organic aerosol (BBOA). While some BBOA constituents generate atmospheric oxidants through photosensitization, a major fraction of BBOA consists of phenolics with negligible or weak absorption of solar radiation. Therefore, these phenolics, together with S(IV), have generally been viewed as atmospheric substrates of other oxidants. Here, we show that their photochemical interactions constitute an efficient source of brown carbon (BrC) and organosulfur products. Under simulated solar irradiation, aqueous S(IV) photochemistry initiates the decay of non/weakly light-absorbing phenolic BB tracers, including phenols, methoxyphenols, and catechols, with methoxyphenols (guaiacol, GUA; and syringol, SYR) exhibiting the most substantial decay. S(IV) photooxidation generates sulfur-centered radicals, which trigger the formation of organosulfur and BrC products, including quinone-like photosensitizers. Scavenging experiments and kinetic modeling demonstrate that triplets (3PS*)-mediated pathways arising from BrC photosensitization dominate the methoxyphenol decay, in turn leading to new BrC formation. Model results reveal that, across varying atmospheric GUA and S(IV) precursor levels, these 3PS* reach 10–15–10–14 M, comparable to those originating from primary photosensitizers in aqueous-phase BBOA. This work identifies a previously overlooked source of photosensitizers and extends the role of non/weakly light-absorbing BB tracers from passive substrates to active contributors to atmospheric oxidative capacity.

articles.title:
Correspondence on
“Kidney Urate Underexcretion
Mediates the Relationship between Per- and Polyfluoroalkyl Substances
and their Alternatives and Uric Acid Levels: Evidence from a Case–Control
Study and an Animal Study”

Dynamic
Reconstitution of Fe–In Dual-Atom Sites
with Bridged Intermediate Adsorption for Selectively Electrochemical
Oxygen Reduction to Hydroxyl Radicals
articles.abstract: Abstract The three-electron (3e–) oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) to hydroxyl radicals (HO•) represents an emerging strategy for water purification, yet achieving high selectivity remains challenging due to the scaling relationships between oxygen-containing intermediates. Herein, we report a Fe–In dual-atom catalyst (FeIn-DAC) with unique d-p orbital hybridization to tailor the electronic structure of Fe–In pairs for triggering optimal oxygen-bridged adsorption. Operando XANES and in situ Raman spectroscopy reveal that the initial Fe–N4 motif dynamically reconstitutes into Fe–N3 as the genuine active site upon ORR initiation, exposing more unsaturated sites for Yeager-type bridge-adsorbed *O–O* species. DFT calculations confirm that charge rearrangement within Fe–In pairs avoids excessively strong or weak electronic coupling with oxygen intermediates for steering 3e– ORR to HO•. As expected, the FeIn-DAC electrocatalytic system achieves a high HO• generation rate of 6.02 μmol L–1 min–1 and delivers ∼90% TOC removal for various antibiotic pollutants across wide pH ranges. A pilot flow-through device further verifies its practical applicability for real pharmaceutical wastewater treatment with ∼75%–85% TOC/COD removal during 24 h continuous operation. This study highlights potential-driven dynamic reconstitution of dual-atom catalysts for steering selective multielectron ORR under real working conditions.
